entities.summary:
Miss Fatima, frequently referred to as 'Miss Fatima', was a British-Indian female chess master.

Born in the early 20th century, Miss Fatima rose through the ranks of the British chess scene, becoming the first woman to qualify for the British Chess Championship in 1929.

Her success caught the attention of the chess community, and she went on to compete in international tournaments, including the 1930 World Chess Championship in Warsaw, Poland.

Despite the challenges she faced as a woman in a male-dominated sport, Miss Fatima continued to compete, demonstrating remarkable skill and dedication to the game of chess.

In the years following World War II, Miss Fatima's contributions to the world of chess were largely forgotten, but her legacy as a pioneering female chess player has been rediscovered and celebrated by chess historians and enthusiasts today.
